properties.title: EHRWorld: A Patient-Centric Medical World Model for Long-Horizon Clinical Trajectories

membership.reason: EHRWorld is a sequential patient-centric LLM world model tracking explicit patient state S_t and simulating long-horizon clinical trajectories under sequential inquiries and interventions.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 action/intervention-conditioned clinical trajectory world model (WT_EHR, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: Causal sequential LLM-based set conditional generator with dual-mode inquiry/intervention prediction

properties.flow: Patient state S_t + clinical action set A_t -> EHRWorld dual-mode prediction -> history update H_{t+1} -> multi-round simulation

properties.purpose: Long-horizon inpatient clinical state simulation under sequential inquiries and interventions.
properties.environment: EHRWorld-110K derived from MIMIC-IV (579 held-out test episodes)

assertions.rationale: Explicit physiological timestamps tau_t and chronological event ordering.
Stratified held-out episode split (579 episodes) and causal chronological ordering.
Explicit patient state S_t = <tau_t, d, Y, H_t> updated deterministically after each step.
Conditioned on full accumulated interaction history H_t.
Distinguishes passive inquiry events (A_inq) from active clinical intervention events (A_int).
Causal sequential set-based conditional LLM generator.

Future physiological and clinical states are predicted conditioned on concurrent passive inquiry (84,010 events) and active intervention (25,798 events) action sets A_t across 579 held-out MIMIC-IV episodes, achieving Avg Score 0.755-0.765 (EHRWorld-4B/8B/14B) vs GPT-5.2 0.618 (Tables 1-2, pp. 6-8). Associational factual-trajectory conditioning only; not causal identification.

Both one-step (next-step teacher-forced) and full-trajectory autoregressive rollouts are quantitatively evaluated in Tables 1-2 (pp. 6-7): EHRWorld-14B achieves Next-Step Numer. S@25 = 0.806, Stat F1 = 0.784, Label F1 = 0.928 (Overall 0.839) and Full-Trajectory S@25 = 0.716, SMAPE = 0.262, Stat F1 = 0.667, Label F1 = 0.913 (Avg Score 0.765, Retention Rate 92.6%).
Long-horizon multi-round simulation error and clinically sensitive event accuracy vs GPT-5.2 and LLM baselines on 579 held-out MIMIC-IV episodes.

evidence_fragments.content: To address this limitation, we introduce EHRWorld, a patient-centric medical world model trained under a causal sequential paradigm, together with EHRWorld-110K, a large-scale longitudinal clinical dataset derived from real-world electronic health records. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that EHRWorld significantly outperforms naive LLM-based baselines, achieving more stable long-horizon simulation, improved modeling of clinically sensitive events, and favorable reasoning efficiency, highlighting the necessity of training on causally grounded, temporally evolving clinical data for reliable and robust medical world modeling.

Figure 2: Overview of the EHRWorld framework. (a) Data construction pipeline. Raw EHR records from MIMIC-IV are processed into the EHRWorld-110K dataset by integrating static patient context with longitudinal clinical events. (b) The EHRWorld model. At each step, the model conditions on the current patient state and a set of clinical actions, generates outcomes via a dual-mode mechanism for inquiries and interventions, and updates the interaction history for sequential trajectory simulation.

This procedure yields a held-out test set of 579 hospitalization episodes, comprising 84,010 inquiry events and 25,798 intervention events, and includes 1,043 unique primary and secondary diagnostic conditions, ensuring a comprehensive representation of various clinical scenarios.

evidence_fragments.content: To test this capability, we evaluate full trajectory prediction, where the model must autoregressively generate the entire hospitalization trajectory from admission to discharge, conditioned on sequential clinical events and interventions.

locator.section_or_table: Section 5.3 Next-Step vs. Full Trajectory Prediction

evidence_fragments.content:
We evaluate model performance in two distinct settings: next-step prediction, where the model predicts the state at t+1 conditioned on ground-
truth history, and full-trajectory simulation, where predictions are generated autoregressively.
EHRWorld-14B achieves a superior overall retention rate of 92.6%, surpassing the best baseline, GPT-5.2 (86.2%).

capability_assessments.rationale: EHRWorld implements persistent explicit patient state S_t = <tau_t, d, Y, H_t> updated deterministically (019) with learned sequential LLM set-conditional dynamics (041, 042), and evaluates both next-step and full-trajectory autoregressive predictions conditioned on sequential clinical inquiry and intervention actions across 579 held-out MIMIC-IV episodes (043, 053; Tables 1-2, Retention Rate 92.6%), supporting L2. No matched counterfactual action comparison (L3) or policy optimization (L4) is evaluated.

limitations: Single-center MIMIC-IV cohort only; no external hospital validation or prospective clinical deployment.

Episode-level diagnostic context Y in S_t is extracted from discharge summaries (Sec 4.1, p. 4), creating a temporal-availability/leakage caveat for prospective real-time clinical simulation; action-conditioned evaluation covers factual trajectories only without causal identification or matched counterfactual comparisons.
notes: All 14 physical PDF pages extracted/read; pages 1 and 4 visually inspected via rendered PNGs.

legacy_cells.O: Hospitalized patients across 1,043 unique primary and secondary diagnostic conditions
legacy_cells.S: Can a model maintain accurate, stable patient-state trajectories across hospitalization while responding to sequential clinical inquiries and interventions?
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Structured, time-stamped EHR events (inquiry measurements, medication administrations, procedures); static demographics and hierarchical diagnoses extracted from discharge summaries
legacy_cells.AT: Append event set to prior interaction history: Ht+1 = Ht ∪ {Et}; update state to ⟨τt+1, d, Y, Ht+1⟩
legacy_cells.AZ: Explicit state tuple: timestamp, static demographics, diagnostic profile, and ordered interaction history
legacy_cells.BA: Persistent state/history update: append each event set and condition subsequent predictions on the complete prior event sequence
legacy_cells.BN: Dual-mode event structure separates passive inquiry events from state-altering interventions; chronological causal masking
legacy_cells.BS: Inquiry outcomes are generated as explicit measurement values; intervention events receive an empty immediate outcome and update subsequent simulation context
legacy_cells.BV: Negative log-likelihood of ground-truth inquiry observations; outcome prediction conditioned on event sets with causal masking
legacy_cells.CD: Full hospitalization trajectory, from admission to discharge (no fixed numeric horizon stated)
legacy_cells.DQ: EHRWorld-110K: 110,513 hospitalization episodes and approximately 17.5 million clinical events; held-out test set: 579 episodes
legacy_cells.DX: Next-step EHRWorld-14B: Numerical S@25 0.806; Stat F1 0.784; Label F1 0.928; Overall 0.839
legacy_cells.DY: Full-trajectory EHRWorld-14B: Numerical S@25 0.716; Stat F1 0.667; Label F1 0.913; Overall 0.765; retention rate 92.6%
legacy_cells.EG: EHRWorld-14B full-case generation latency: 1.29 seconds per case; peak throughput: 23,318 tokens/second
legacy_cells.EI: Non-WM LLM baselines: GPT-5.2 Avg Score 0.618 and Gemini-3.0-Pro-Preview 0.574; EHRWorld models 0.755–0.765
legacy_cells.EK: Hyperparameter sensitivity/ablation: learning-rate and training-epoch comparisons for EHRWorld-14B
legacy_cells.EL: Residual inaccuracies can propagate over extended autoregressive rollouts; naive LLM baselines show state inconsistency and error drift under sequential interventions
legacy_cells.EO: EHRWorld-110K records are described as de-identified and processed in compliance with established privacy and data-protection standards
legacy_cells.FB: Structured patient state comprising timestamp, static demographics, diagnostic profile, and chronological clinical-event history
legacy_cells.FL: Fine-tuned Qwen LLM receives patient demographics, diagnoses, timestamp, and ordered EHR history; conditions outcome generation on sets of inquiry/intervention events; generates inquiry values and appends event outcomes to history; no planner is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces the EHRWorld-110K longitudinal EHR dataset and EHRWorld patient-centric simulator, and evaluates long-horizon trajectory fidelity and stability against LLM baselines.
legacy_cells.FN: EHRWorld-14B full-trajectory results: S@25 0.716, SMAPE 0.262, Stat F1 0.667, Label F1 0.913, Avg Score 0.765; next-to-full overall retention 92.6%.
legacy_cells.FO: Autoregressive generation can propagate residual inaccuracies over extended rollouts; evaluation focuses on trajectory fidelity/stability and does not assess treatment optimization, policy learning, or real-world decision support.
legacy_cells.FP: Extend evaluation to decision-centric settings, counterfactual treatment comparison, and clinician-in-the-loop studies.
legacy_cells.FQ: Prior patient simulators are described as relying on static case descriptions and lacking dynamic, intervention-aware patient-state transitions, leading to inconsistency across sequential interactions.
legacy_cells.FR: Action-conditioned retrospective trajectory fidelity does not establish causal identification or treatment-effect validity. No alternative-action counterfactual comparison, treatment/policy optimization, prospective/external validation, clinician evaluation, or clinical utility outcome is reported.
